Worst 'Japanese' food
Mar 2019 • Couples
My girlfriend and I visited with high expectations having read very positive reviews. To our disappointment, the only thing that made the bill justifiable was the excellent interior design.

Customer service: Poor
We had to ask repeatedly for our Sake to be served even after our first dish had arrived.

Food: Terrible
Sashimi was frozen. Every bite I took I was welcomed with a rush of water.

Prawn tempura was deep fried prawns at best.

Soft shell crab maki - the soft shell crab was most definitely deep fried previously and upon close inspection, all the meat of the crab had been removed and all the was left was the 'soft shell.

Aburi set - as difficult as this dish may be to make to a high standard, all they did was get a blow torch, blow it on the fish a bit and serve. I can’t even say they seared it.

I love Japanese food. I would eat low budget or high budget Japanese meals even if it's to a low quality and be happy with it since I love Japanesw food.

But this is the first time I’ve had to leave a review, let alone a negative one since the combination of poor food, customer service and pricing has left my girlfriend and I regretting our visit and wishing we should've just stuck to our local Vietnamese restaurant that delivers 100x more flavour and value for money.

Just a friendly reminder to any future visitors that we highly DO NOT RECOMMEND this restaurant.

For the other reviews that say this is place is great, they have either never had good Japanese food or they may be right in saying that it is the best Japanese food in Saigon. If the latter is the case, I may shed a tear for any Japanese person that may visit this city and want a taste of home.

Nice atmosphere, good food, reasonable prices
Jan 2019 • Couples
My wife and I had the pleasure of dining at Saiko Sushi this past weekend. Although sushi restaurants are abundant in HCMC, we selected this restaurant mainly due to its location, close to our residence and other positive reviews. It didn’t disappoint. We were greeted by a friendly staff a little after 7 PM, to virtually an empty restaurant. Once seated, we noticed the surroundings and atmosphere quite appealing and the customers soon began pouring in. The menu was extensive with too many choices to even consider as they all sounded and looked delicious. The menu covered everything from sushi, sashimi, the Chefs specialty and signature rolls and even “hot pots”. We elected to order a specialty roll and two of the same “sushi dinners/platters”. The roll was served within minutes and a few minutes later, out came one of the sushi plates. We were a bit confused as only the one plate was served (although we had ordered two), which we decided to dig in immediately. It was very good. Communicating with the staff was a little difficult as their English wasn’t the best and our Vietnamese language skills are non-existent. We weren’t sure is we miscommunicated our order or, since the entrees were the same, maybe they were helping us pace ourselves. After resting and talking a few minutes, we soon realized that we had more than enough food to fill us up and the second plate really wasn’t necessary. Just as soon as we came to that conclusion, out came the second entree! We were prepared to take what was left home but needless to say, we (actually, I) had no problem finishing the entire entree. The meal was delicious, the sushi prices very reasonable (the sashimi prices were quite a bit higher) and service a little slow once we were ready for the check. I don’t think that is specific to this restaurant as I find that to be the norm at almost every restaurant I have eaten at in HCMC. Overall, it was an enjoyable evening, great food and we will return.

A gem!

I have been a regular patron of Ichiba Sushi Restaurant in HCMC until i discovered Saiko Sushi near my hotel. The staffs are conversant in English and the place is regularly patronized by locals and foreigners (Japanese and Koreans). If you wonder if it's an expensive place catered to foreigners, I would disagree. The quality of the food is fabulous and value for money. Throw in good service and ambience (Tenka music, classic Japanese gardens) and walla, Saiko Sushi. I visited a few times on each stay in HCMC without fail.
